likelyCauses: Missing normalization for the 1170×2532 iOS canvas versus the 342×320 Android crop, so CSS points or platform text metrics are being converted to raw pixels without an equivalent scale.
Platform-default font metrics or font weight resolution differ between Android and iOS.
Text ellipsis and available-row-width calculations vary by platform.
Shared component padding or margins are not being specified in device-independent units.

suggestedFixes: Define an explicit scale mapping between the iOS and Android test canvases and compare normalized component bounds rather than raw image dimensions.
Standardize font family, size, weight, and line-height tokens across platforms, then verify computed text widths.
Use one deterministic ellipsis implementation and fixed row/content widths on both platforms.
Set shared horizontal padding and margin constants in dp/pt, including section headers, member rows, composer controls, and the selected-row highlight.
Capture the iOS UI in a crop with the same logical component bounds as Android before running isomorphism checks.

Map the in-progress download action to the cancel icon in both platforms, or render the download icon only on idle state in both.

summary: Android renders the entire dialog content in a more vertically compressed layout, causing fields to appear narrower and more cramped than the React baseline.
Android shows the Cancel and Create Agent action buttons overlaying/floating above the API URL input area, while React places them cleanly below the form content.
Android version crops/clips the API KEY field — only a thin top sliver is visible at the bottom edge, whereas React shows the full field with a value row.
Typography on Android appears heavier/bolder in the banner ('Agent limit reached (2/2 on Free plan). Upgrade for more') with bold styling, while React renders it in regular weight.
Android adds a visible '(optional)' suffix to the DESCRIPTION label in lighter weight; React omits this suffix.
likelyCauses: Android Compose dialog is using intrinsic/default component sizing instead of matching the React design tokens (heights, paddings, font weights).
Action row (Cancel/Create Agent) is being rendered as a sticky/overlapping footer or in an incorrect container, causing it to float over form fields rather than sit below.
Form content exceeds viewport height on Android without internal scroll, clipping the API KEY field at the bottom edge.
Bold/regular font weight mapping differs between React (CSS) and Android (Compose TextStyle) for the upgrade banner and labels.
Description label includes locale-specific '(optional)' suffix on Android that is not present in React's label string.
suggestedFixes: Increase Android input field heights and vertical spacing to match React design tokens (likely 48–56dp inputs with 16–20dp field gaps).
Fix action button placement: render Cancel/Create Agent as a sticky footer below scrollable form content, not overlaid on top of the API URL field.
Add internal scrolling (Modifier.verticalScroll) to the dialog body so all fields including API KEY remain reachable at 390×844.
Normalize font weights: render the upgrade banner text in regular/medium weight (not bold), and ensure section labels use the same weight scale as React.
Remove '(optional)' from DESCRIPTION label on Android, or unify label rendering across platforms to use identical copy.
intentional: The 'ANDROID' vs 'REACT' label badges in the upper-right are test harness annotations and not part of the UI.
The metadata caption at the bottom (RGB similarity, pixel perfect, mismatch) is test infrastructure output and not a UI element.

summary: Android side renders as a centered modal dialog on a dark gray overlay, while React renders as a full-page panel with a yellow header banner.

Avatar component using fixed dp sizing that doesn't scale equivalently across the two render targets.
Tag/pill background colors defined with different opacity or color tokens per platform (or rendered with different color-management).
analysis.suggestedOwner: Kuikly mobile thread component owner (message-row + markdown rendering)
suggestedFixes: Normalize the message-row container background color across platforms; ensure the same theme token is applied on iOS so the cream fill is present.
Pin a consistent text font stack or explicit font-weight values so 'task', '#607', and '@Android-Developer-2' bold weights match between iOS and Android.
Replace the glyph used as the timestamp separator with a platform-neutral character (e.g. '·' U+00B7) or ensure the icon font is bundled on iOS to prevent fallback substitution to 'K'.
Constrain avatar size to a shared dp token so the icon box dimensions match across Android and iOS renderings.
Audit the color tokens for inline-code/task pills ('#607', '#对话流专修') so identical hex/opacity values are used on both platforms; verify via screenshot diff at 100% zoom.
intentional: The higher iOS canvas resolution (1170x2532 vs 260x844) is expected and not a divergence to fix.
Different native font families between Android and iOS are intentional platform defaults, but their effect on wrap and weight should be normalized via tokens.
